div.div: Who owns what. Terraform creates each function with a first package, its role, its triggers, the live alias, the deployment group and the alarms, and ignores later code and alias changes. The application pipeline owns the code and moves the alias.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 626px; height: 1px; padding-top: 888px; margin-left: 668px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #232F3E;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #232F3E; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Rollback. Platform, point the environment to the previous module tag and run the same deploy. Functions, CodeDeploy moves the alias back during the canary, or a manual release of the previous version moves it later. Data never rolls back, so changes keep the old version working.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 606px; height: 1px; padding-top: 888px; margin-left: 1328px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #232F3E;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #232F3E; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Secrets. No pipeline holds an access key, since every job assumes a role through OIDC. VPN keys and third-party keys live in Secrets Manager, and Terraform and function settings hold only their ARN. Saved plans stay in the private state bucket.
